title: The gnomes and the pickaxe
summary: The gnomes in R.E.P.O. arrive as a group rather than one at a time: a director keeps them, each one moves at a speed between a minimum and a maximum, and a pickaxe warns you before it lands.
body: The gnomes are not a single monster. A director keeps them as a set rather than as one creature, so a level can hold several at once and the game can decide when each of them acts.
Each gnome has a speed range. There is a lowest and a highest speed rather than one value, so two gnomes of the same kind do not move at exactly the same rate.
They keep out of each other's way. There is a collider for avoiding and an offset for backing away, which is how a group can crowd a player without standing inside one another.

The director thinks in pauses. It has a short idle and a long idle of its own, alongside a list of the gnomes it is managing and a current state, so much of what a gnome does is decided between actions rather than during them.
Interacting with one is not instant. The animation system keeps a pickaxe tell and a pickaxe hit as separate sounds, so the swing warns you before it lands.
A gnome is audible from the moment it appears. There are sounds for spawning and despawning, footsteps, short and long movement, a jump and a landing, and a notice sound for when it spots you.
Impacts come in three weights. Light, medium and heavy sounds are kept apart, which is how the same collision can sound like a nudge or like a hit.

Being stunned is a state with an entrance and an exit: there is a stun sound and a separate sound for coming out of it, along with a small behaviour of its own for the moment it is thrown after being stunned.
What this entry does not tell you: how many gnomes a level may hold, how much damage a pickaxe does, or how long the pauses are. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: A director keeps the gnomes as a set, with a list of them and a state of its own.
The director has a short idle and a long idle.
Each gnome moves at a speed between a minimum and a maximum.
They have a collider for avoiding each other and an offset for backing away.
The pickaxe has a tell and a hit as separate sounds.
There are sounds for spawning and despawning, footsteps, short and long movement, a jump, a landing and noticing a player.
facts.evidence: identifiers: soundSpawn, soundDespawn, soundFootstep, soundMoveShort, soundMoveLong, soundJump, soundLand, soundNotice

facts.claim: Impacts come in light, medium and heavy versions.
Being stunned has an entrance and an exit sound, and there is a small thrown-while-stunned behaviour of its own.
A gnome keeps a state, a rotation spring, death effects and sounds for being hurt and dying.
facts.evidence: identifiers: currentState, rotationSpring, deathEffects, soundHurt, soundDeath

facts.claim: Its animations are named one by one: idle, attack, despawn, falling, idle breaker, jump, land, move and a move outro, with a pickaxe animation beside them.
facts.evidence: asset names: Enemy Gnome Idle, Enemy Gnome Attack, Enemy Gnome Despawn, Enemy Gnome Falling, Enemy Gnome Idle Breaker, Enemy Gnome Jump, Enemy Gnome Land, Enemy Gnome Move, Enemy Gnome Move Outro, ANIM PICKAXE
